Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testLargeSample()` in `PolynomialFitterTest` attempts to fit polynomials of degrees 0 to 9 to a large sample of 40,000 data points each. The test uses `PolynomialFitter`, which internally uses a multivariate vector optimizer (LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer) that is known from the current bug report to suffer from severe inefficiencies when handling large numbers of weights. The bug report describes that when a large number of weights is passed to multivariate vector optimizers through the `Weight` class, the implementation internally creates and copies an nxn full matrix from an n-elements vector, which causes huge memory consumption and can exhaust memory for large n.

In this test, many points (40,000) are added with weight 1.0, resulting in a large number of weights, triggering the problematic matrix creation and copy in the optimizer. This inefficiency leads to excessive memory usage and test failures on large datasets, exactly as the bug report states.

Examining the relevant code snippets for `PolynomialFitter.fit(double[] guess)` reveals it simply calls the generic `fit` method passing a `PolynomialFunction.Parametric` and the initial guess, implying the problem lies deeper at the optimizer or the weighted points handling level. The `CurveFitter.addObservedPoint(double weight, double x, double y)` method confirms points are wrapped as `WeightedObservedPoint` with weight, enabling the optimizer to receive many weights.

No recent issues directly relate to this numerical or memory problem. The issue is rooted in the weight handling in the multivariate vector optimizer used indirectly by `PolynomialFitter`.

Summary: The test fails due to the underlying optimizer's inefficient handling of a large number of weighted points, which leads to excessive memory consumption and resource exhaustion when fitting large samples. This inefficiency originates from the optimizer creating large n×n matrices internally even when only a vector of weights is conceptually needed.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
